title: Why Premium Apps Feel Like Lego, Not Magic
subtitle: You don't code maps and email from scratch — you plug in specialists.
intro: Your app needs maps, logins, chat, email, and fast images. Building all five yourself would take months. Premium apps cheat — in a smart way.
takeaway: Use specialist APIs to feel premium fast, but remember every API is a dependency you pay for and must handle when it fails.

sections.heading: Everyday analogy: a food truck with helpers
sections.body:
Think of your app like a food truck. You cook the main dish, but you hire helpers for the rest.

One helper draws your beautiful menu board. Another handles payments. Another delivers flyers. You focus on food, they handle their specialty.

APIs are those helpers for apps. Next, see why you need them.

sections.heading: Why does this exist?: don't rebuild what experts do best
sections.body:
Why does this exist? Because some features are hard to build well.

An API is a ready-made service your app can call. Instead of building maps, email, or login from zero, you plug one in:
- Mapbox for custom maps and real-time location
- Clerk for login and user management with polished UI
- Resend for transactional email that avoids spam folders
- Stream for chat, feeds, and video
- Cloudinary for image and video optimization via CDN

You ship faster and it looks premium. But helpers can cause problems.

sections.heading: What can go wrong: when helpers cost or quit
sections.body:
What can go wrong? Every helper adds risk.

If you add five APIs, you have five bills, five places that can go down, and five sets of user data leaving your app.

If Mapbox is slow, your maps are slow. If Resend fails, no password emails go out. If you send every image through Cloudinary without limits, costs spike.

So use APIs for hard, non-core features, and always plan for failure.

steps.narration: You build only your core app idea.
You call Mapbox when you need a custom map.
Clerk handles login so you don't store passwords badly.
Resend sends the welcome email reliably.
Stream adds chat without you building real-time servers.
Cloudinary optimizes and delivers images fast via CDN.

quiz.q: What is an API in this lesson?
options: A ready-made service your app can call for a specific job
A new programming language for premium apps
A design tool that only makes logos
A database you must host yourself
quiz.why: APIs like Mapbox or Clerk are specialist services you plug in instead of building from scratch.

quiz.q: Why would you use Clerk instead of building login yourself?
options: To get polished UI and secure user management faster
To make your maps look better
quiz.why: Clerk is the auth specialist from the saves — it saves time and security mistakes.

quiz.q: What breaks first if usage grows 100x and you use 5 APIs without limits?
options: Costs spike and one API failure can break your app
Your app automatically gets faster for free
You no longer need to write any code
quiz.why: Every API is a dependency with bills and downtime — scale makes cost and failure handling critical.

extra: APIs often have free tiers then usage-based pricing — monitor calls to avoid surprise bills.
